title: The twists $\mathcal O(d)$ exist
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $d\in\mathbf Z$, and let
$U_0,U_1,U_{01}$ be the standard affine cover of
$\mathbf P^1_k$ of [def-sc-p1-standard]. Then a twisted
structure sheaf $\mathcal O(d)$ as in
[def-sc-p1-standard] exists, and it is an
invertible
$\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1_k}$-module; it is unique up to unique
isomorphism compatible with the generating sections $g_0,g_1$.

proof.text: Obtain L and TwistData T from the construction-only gluing lemma. This isolates the local free-module construction and cocycle argument, without assuming invertibility or any uniqueness conclusion.

For a generator s on an open U, form the compatible family of all its restrictions. The unitHomEquiv of Mathlib gives multiplication by s as a morphism from the structure sheaf on Over U. Bijectivity on every subopen, supplied by TwistData, gives a componentwise linear isomorphism and hence an isomorphism of sheaves. Transport this through overEquiv and restrictFunctorIsoPullback. The two standard charts cover P¹, so each point has a neighbourhood on which L pulls back to the structure sheaf. This proves Scheme.Modules.IsInvertible L.

For another TwistData T′ on L′, compose the inverse of the local generator isomorphism for L with the one for L′ on each chart. On an arbitrary subopen of the overlap, write a source section as a•g₀. Restrict TwistData.map_g₀ to this subopen; it rewrites the section as (a u₀₁)•g₁. Both local morphisms send it to a•g′₀=(a u₀₁)•g′₁. Thus the local morphisms agree. Apply the morphism-gluing clause to produce f:L→L′ preserving both generators; repeat in the other direction to produce g:L′→L.

Two global morphisms with source L that agree on g₀ and g₁ agree after restriction to each chart: naturality gives agreement on all restricted generators and linearity plus the surjectivity fields of TwistData gives agreement on every section. The separation clause of the gluing theorem then gives equality. Apply this criterion to fg and gf versus the identities; the generator-preserving equations show both composites are identities. Package f and g as an isomorphism, and apply the same equality criterion to the hom of any other generator-preserving isomorphism. Iso.ext proves uniqueness.
